knownGaps.evidence: The Syncfusion EJ2 switch 'change' event emits the payload { checked, event, name } only. Confirmed three ways: (1) source node_modules/@syncfusion/ej2-buttons/src/switch/switch.js:97 builds changeEventArgs = { checked, event }; (2) the generated discovery artifact discovery/event-payload-surface.json lists ChangeEventArgs members as checked, event, name with no isInteracted; (3) a live browser capture on /Sandbox/Components/Switch of the real change payload after a trusted toggle returned keys [checked, event, name], hasIsInteracted=false. The runtime event-fusion.ts adapter passes the vendor args through unchanged and injects nothing. So FusionSwitchChangeArgs.IsInteracted is always undefined at runtime and has no observable behavior; no fails-when-broken test can exist for it.
knownGaps.whyNotMapped: BDD Rule 3 forbids a test that still passes when the member is broken — IsInteracted is already effectively broken (never populated), so any assertion would be a pass-hack. Removing the unbacked property from the slice (the skill's prescribed correction) edits Alis.Reactive.Fusion/Components/FusionSwitch/Events/FusionSwitchOnChanged.cs, which the CARDINAL RULE forbids. This is a framework-slice onboarding defect outside this task's edit scope, reported rather than faked.
